definition: Everything that exists: all of space and all the matter and energy in it, including many billions of galaxies.
The stretching of electromagnetic radiation to a longer observed wavelength, because the star or galaxy that emitted it is moving away from the observer.
The theory that the Universe began billions of years ago from a single, extremely hot and dense point, and has been expanding ever since.

Microwave radiation (CMBR) of a particular frequency that reaches us from every direction in space; it was produced shortly after the Universe formed and has since been stretched to microwave wavelengths by the expansion.
The speed $v$ at which a galaxy recedes from the Earth divided by its distance $d$ from the Earth, $H_0 = \frac{v}{d}$; its current estimate is $2.2 \times 10^{-18}$ per second.
The time since the Big Bang, estimated as $\frac{1}{H_0} = \frac{d}{v}$, which comes to about 14 billion years.
